newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: High oil prices to erase Venezuela '96 fiscal gap.
newsitem.headline: High oil prices to erase Venezuela '96 fiscal gap.

text.p: The Venezuelan government expects to end 1996 with no fiscal deficit thanks to a recent rise in oil prices following U.S. military intervention in Iraq, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Friday.
"There will practically be no deficit for Venezuela in 1996," Matos told a news conference.
The Venezuelan government had set a target to reduce its deficit from seven to 3.3 percent of gross domestic product this year in a stand-by loan agreement with the International Monetary Fund.
But better-than-expected oil prices have virtually wiped out that deficit, Matos said.
Venezuela's basket of oil and crudes have averaged $17.23 per barrel so far this year, up from initial government estimates of just $13.50 per barrel.
Matos stressed that unforeseen revenues from the surge in oil prices will go to a special account and that some will be used to pay off foreign debt.
